cards: **B1 · Mapping AAV capsid-receptor interactions to explain barrier transcytosis versus intracellular retention.** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: not the lever · halted: cost record broken **Question.** Which capsid-receptor binding signatures distinguish AAV variants that transcytose brain microvascular endothelial cells from those retained inside, and can a model predict this? **What is known.** A published in-silico AAV design method (ALICE) mapped receptor binding and CNS tropism for 6,387 capsid sequences [src_alice]; it never separated transcytosis from endothelial retention. No published dataset matches computed capsid-receptor binding signatures to transcytosis versus intracellular retention in brain endothelial cells at more than a handful of capsids [src_merkel2016]. **Hypothesis.** Capsid-receptor binding signatures, not sequence alone, will classify which variants cross brain endothelium because receptor engagement drives transcytosis [src_tfr1_2023]. **Restructuring.** Adaptive selection rounds: each of four rounds waits on the previous model before scoring its 250 pairs. Pair signatures do not depend on the model, so all four rounds' pairs are scored in one batch instead of sequentially. **If compute is the lever.** At 4,000 scored pairs accuracy reaches >=0.80, beating 1,000 pairs by >=0.10; batching takes 16 hours versus 64 for four sequential rounds. **If not.** Accuracy stays <=0.65 at 250, 1,000 and 4,000 pairs; sequential selection hits that ceiling at 1,000 pairs, so batching buys speed only. **Test.** Score 250, 1,000, 4,000 capsid-receptor pairs for binding signatures; classify published transcytosis versus retention under leave-one-capsid-family-out folds against sequence-only and affinity-rank baselines; time batch scoring versus four-round sequential scoring and side-by-side copies. *Compute axis.* Capsid-receptor pair signature evaluations the answer needs: 250–4,000 pair evaluations, 3 levels. Closest prior: 6,387 [src_alice]. **Check first.** Predicted AAV1-AAVR contacts match published cryo-EM residues, and batch scoring matches four-round sequential accuracy within 0.03 [src_zhang2019]. Tolerance: contact-residue recall >=0.80 within 5 Angstrom; correct AAV1-over-AAV2 affinity order; |batch minus sequential| balanced accuracy <=0.03. **Would not show.** Labels come from few published capsids, so accuracy intervals are wide. Predicted signatures are structural approximations, not measured affinities. filesystem.page_text: Filesystems are billed per GiB used per month in one-hour increments. For example, at a rate of $0.20 per GiB per month: If you use 1,000 GiB continuously for a full month (720 hours), you'll be billed $200.00. If you use 1,000 GiB continuously for a full day (24 hours), you'll be billed $6.67. Important: The rate above is used for example purposes and might not reflect current pricing. The actual price will be displayed when you create your filesystem.
